newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SCOTTISH CLUBS GAMBLE ON FOREIGN TALENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCOTTISH CLUBS GAMBLE ON FOREIGN TALENT.

text.p: Many of the Scottish premier division clubs have cashed in on the strength of the pound by buying abroad.
Saturday's start to the championship will give an early indication of whether the money has been wisely spent.

Rich or poor, almost every manager preferred the continental flavour to home-grown produce. Of the 33 major signings, 19 were foreign, with champions Rangers setting the trend, splashing out 15 million pounds ($24.5 million) on eight new players -- none British.

Manager Walter Smith spent most of his summer converting pounds to lire, luring five men from serie A -- Sergio Porrini, a four million pounds ($6.5 million) recruit from Juventus, Lorenzo Amoruso from Fiorentina at a similar price, Perugia striker Marco Negri cost 3.7 million ($6 million), while teenager Rino Gatuso and Swedish midfielder Jonas Thern were picked up as free agents from Perugia and Roma respectively.
Smith now has 15 foreign players at Ibrox and it is possible for Rangers to field a side on Monday night, when they launch their defence at home to Hearts, which does not contain a single Scot.

The Rangers manager is unrepentant about his failure to buy British, saying: "The standard of people that Rangers require is not really available in Scotland or England, or if they are, the transfer fee is too high. I had to go abroad to buy players."

Across Glasgow, rivals Celtic have bought Swedish striker Henrik Larsson from Feyenoord and French defender Stephane Mahe from Rennes. However, as if to underline Smith's point, the 650,000 pounds ($1.1 million) fee that was paid for each player is dwarfed by the four million ($6.5 million) to obtain Scottish internationals Darren Jackson from Hibs and Craig Burley from Chelsea.

Other clubs followed in Smith's footsteps, with Dundee United buying Swedish striker Goran Marklund, Hearts signing Stephane Adam of Metz and Thomas Flogel of Austria Vienna, while Edinburgh rivals, Hibernian, picked up Jean-Marc Boco from Lens in France and Icelandic international keeper Olafur Gottskalsson.

Rangers have already been made clear favourites to win their 10th title in a row which puts immense pressure on Celtic's new coach, Dutchman Wim Jansen, who has replaced Tommy Burns. His task is to end that monopoly and satisfy the demands of Celtic's colossal support -- 41,000 turned up in midweek to watch them against Welsh minnows Inter CableTel in a UEFA Cup tie.
Celtic open their campaign on Sunday away to Hibernian, where Darren Jackson may have to run a gauntlet of hate from his old fans who were unhappy about his sale.
"I don't know what kind of reception I'll get but I'm not bothered. I knew I had to go back sometime, so it's good to get the game over and done with," the player said.
On Saturday, Aberdeen -- whose five summer purchases were all British -- face Scottish Cup holders Kilmarnock, promoted St Johnstone open at home to Dundee United and Dunfermline face Motherwell.
